$$

&\text{S} \rightarrow \% a \text{T} \mid \text{U} !\\
&\text{T} \rightarrow a \text{S} \mid b a \text{T} \mid \epsilon\\
&\text{U} \rightarrow \# a \text{TU} \mid \epsilon\\
\end{aligned}
$$

options.text:

$\text{S}:\{\%, \#, !\}$

$\text{U}:\{\#, \epsilon\}$

The $\text{FOLLOW}$ sets for each of the nonterminals $\mathrm{S}, \mathrm{T}, \mathrm{U}$ is as follows :
$\text{S}:\{\#, !, \$\}$

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|}\hline\; \textbf {Grammar} & \quad \textbf {Semantic Rules} \\\hline \mathrm{E}_1 \rightarrow \mathrm{E}_2+\mathrm{T} & \mathrm{E}_1 \text {.string }=\mathrm{E}_1 \text {.string } \| \text {T.string } \| \text { ‘+' } \\ \mathrm{E}_1 \rightarrow \mathrm{T} & \mathrm{E}_1 \cdot \text {string }=\mathrm{T} \text {.string } \\\mathrm{T}_1 \rightarrow \mathrm{T}_2 * \mathrm{~F} & \mathrm{T}_1 \text {.string }=\mathrm{T}_2 \text {.string } \| \text {F.string } \| \text { ‘*' } \\ \mathrm{T} \rightarrow \mathrm{F} & \text {T.string }=\text {F.string } \\ \mathrm{F} \rightarrow(\mathrm{E}) & \text {F.string }=\text {E.string } \\ \mathrm{F} \rightarrow \text {num} & \text {F.string }=\text { num.string }\\\hline\end{array}$$

The syntax of a propositional calculus can be described by the context-free grammar $\text{G}=\langle \text{V}_n, \text{V}_t, \text{P, S}\rangle$
where $V_n=\{\text{S}\}, \text{V}_t=\{$ not, if, then, and, or, $p, q, r\}$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{P}=&\{\text{S} \rightarrow p, \text{S} \rightarrow q, \text{S} \rightarrow r\\
& \text{S} \rightarrow \text { not } \text{S},\\
& \text{S} \rightarrow \text{if S then S}\\
& \text{S} \rightarrow \text{S or S},\\
&\text{S} \rightarrow \text{S and S}\}
\end{aligned}
$$
Choose the False statements about the above grammar and language :

options.text: "or", "and" are left associative, But not right associative
